This comparison examines the proportion of operated versus non-operated acute patients across national, regional, and hospital levels in Denmark, based on data from the Danish Acute Surgery Database (AKDB) for 2025 [^src1]. Nationally, out of 9,896 total patients, 3,250 (32.84%) underwent surgery, while the majority, 6,646 (67.16%), were treated non-operatively [^src1]. 

Regional analysis reveals significant variation in surgical intervention rates. The Capital Region ([[hovedstaden-region-i-alt|Hovedstaden Region i alt]]) leads with the highest proportion of operated patients at 38.63%, followed by Region Zealand ([[sjaelland-region-i-alt|Sjælland Region i alt]]) at 37.60% [^src1]. In contrast, the North Denmark Region ([[nordjylland-region-i-alt|Nordjylland Region i alt]]) records the lowest regional surgical rate at 23.57% [^src1]. The Region of Southern Denmark ([[syddanmark-region-i-alt|Syddanmark Region i alt]]) and Central Denmark Region ([[midtjylland-region-i-alt|Midtjylland Region i alt]]) fall in the middle at 31.17% and 29.51%, respectively [^src1].

At the hospital level, [[holbaek-sygehus|Holbæk Sygehus]] emerges as the leader with the highest surgical rate among standard somatic hospitals, operating on 45.62% of its 331 patients [^src1]. [[amager-og-hvidovre-hospital|Amager og Hvidovre Hospital]] follows closely at 43.23%, and [[naestved-slagese-og-ringsted-sygehuse|Næstved, Slagelse og Ringsted sygehuse]] at 43.00% [^src1]. Conversely, [[sygehus-lillebaelt|Sygehus Lillebælt]] reports one of the lowest surgical rates among major hospitals at 20.38%, and [[bornholms-hospital|Bornholms Hospital]] operates on only 17.28% of its patients [^src1]. 

Notable outliers include [[aalborg-universitetshospital-thisted|Aalborg Universitetshospital, Thisted]], which reports a 0% surgical rate across 57 patients, and psychiatric units such as Region Hovedstadens Psykiatri (0% of 1 patient) and Psykiatrien Nordjylland (data missing, marked with "#"), which inherently do not perform acute somatic surgeries [^src1]. Because the available evidence consists of only a single dated section, no longitudinal trends regarding changes in surgical versus non-operative management over time can be established.
